subject: Information Theory
title: Spelling and Error Tolerance
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Spelling and Error Tolerance.

hook.text: You read 'teh' as 'the' without even pausing. Your brain fixed the error before you noticed it.

buildup.text: English spelling has enough redundancy that most single-letter errors don't change the recognized word.

discovery.text: Autocorrect works because few misspellings match another real word. The redundancy creates error-correcting distance.

twist.text: Languages with less redundancy would be harder to read in noisy conditions. Every letter would be critical.

climax.text: Spelling rules that seem arbitrary actually create Hamming-like distance between words, aiding recognition.

punchline.text: Messy spelling has a hidden purpose: resilience.

quiz.question: How does spelling redundancy help communication?
options: Misspellings can be corrected because few errors match other words
